results.title: Theoretical and experimental investigation of the 1H NMR spectrum of putrescine - ScienceDirect
results.content: Chemical shifts *δ* and spin–spin coupling constants *J* have been calculated for the putrescine molecule, a polyamine present in prostate tissue, through a DFT/B3LYP/6-311++G(d,p)/PCM/(GIAO) approach, which has been shown to be accurate in previous work. From *δ* and *J* values, calculated for the first time for the isolated and the solvated putrescine, the 1H NMR spectra have been simulated. Comparisons between the calculated and the experimental NMR spectra at 400 MHz show a good agreement and allow to propose reliable values for the NMR spin Hamiltonian parameters of putrescine to be used as good starting values for further quantitation methods of metabolites in prostate tissue. NMR spin Hamiltonian parameters: chemical shifts and spin-coupling constants, accurate enough to simulate a NMR spectrum in good agreement with an *in vitro* experimental one, are proposed for putrescine. We focused on predicting the chemical shifts and the spin–spin coupling constants of isolated and solvated putrescine molecule, and on using these *a priori* values to simulate the NMR spectrum of putrescine for a given magnetic field strength. From calculated chemical shifts *δ* and *J* coupling constants, the theoretical NMR spectrum of putrescine has been obtained following [17] by use of Gabedit [14] handling up to 12 1H nuclear spins in its recent version. Chemical shifts *δ* and spin–spin couplings *J* have been calculated for the first time for the putrescine (isolated and solvated) molecule, within a B3LYP/6-311++G(d,p)/(PCM)/(GIAO) approach. Using these calculated NMR spin parameters leads to a theoretical NMR spectrum of solvated putrescine in good agreement with the experimental one obtained in solution in D2O at 400 MHz. This agreement validates our new data, especially for the yet unknown *J* constants and permits us to propose NMR spin. For the sarcosine molecule (C3H7NO2) in gas phase and in water solution, four calculation steps have been carried out: (1) the determination of stable geometries lying in a given range of relative energy above the lowest one, (2) the determination of the chemical shifts for the protons attached to carbon atoms, (3) the estimation of zero-point vibrational corrections on these chemical shifts, and (4) the simulation of the 1H NMR spectrum of the sarcosine from the calculated 1H chemical shifts.

results.title: The refractive index of silver nanowire networks: a heuristic approach to the foundations of the optical constants, from experiment to theory | Discover Nano
results.content: # The refractive index of silver nanowire networks: a heuristic approach to the foundations of the optical constants, from experiment to theory. The refractive index of silver nanowire networks: a heuristic approach to the foundations of the optical constants, from experiment to theory. This study employs Mie’s scattering theory and van de Hulst’s mixing model to predict the refractive indices (*n*, *k*) of silver nanowire (AgNW) networks in the visible and near-infrared wavelengths, allowing the comparison to the experimentally determined *k* spectra. Determining the refractive indices (RIs) of silver nanowire (AgNW) networks, whether experimentally or theoretically, is challenging. We do however note that the determination of the *effective* refractive index remains useful, as it can allow for the prediction of the optical behavior of the combined (AgNW network/glass) hybrid material, making it valuable for applications in which that specific hybrid’s optical response is of primary interest. showed the good agreement between the theoretical prediction of the ‘Mie + vdH’ model and the optical response of AgNW networks embedded in a transparent polymer matrix over visible wavelengths. The measured optical transmittance and reflectance spectra in the visible and near-infrared wavelengths [300–2500] nm of AgNW networks of varying nanowire density and with different average diameters \(D\_{NW}\) are shown in Fig. 2 (See S1 of the Supplementary Information for more information on experimental methods). A comparison between the theoretical transmittance of the network (\(T\_\text {net}\)) and experimental data demonstrates fair agreement, particularly for networks with larger nanowire diameters (\(D\_\text {NW}\)) and at shorter wavelengths. This constitutes a limitation to the models, not identified before, and which should be explicitly considered when simulating the optical properties of silver nanowire networks with this theoretical framework. Denser networks, characterized by smaller gap sizes, exhibit more metallic-like optical properties, resulting in *n* values closer to those of a silver thin film [45]. These results highlight the nuanced interplay between the structural parameters of nanowire networks and their refractive index behavior, emphasizing the importance of both density and nanowire diameter in the shaping of their optical properties. *et al.* The refractive index of silver nanowire networks: a heuristic approach to the foundations of the optical constants, from experiment to theory.
